title: Money On Your Chest
note: The story serial (src/story_reel.py next): one part a day, in order. Part 1 is the owner's story (2026-11-14); parts 2 to 8 were written on their word, 'create the story yourself part 2, 3, 4, etc... post them one a day'. Every company, person and stock in it is made up. 'posted' marks a part that went out by hand; state/story.json on the server keeps the rest. To carry on after the last part: take 'last' off it, give it a cliffhanger, and add parts.

cast.the narrator (I): grey-blue shirt #8a96ab, dark blue trousers #2e3a52, brown hair #6b4426, skin #f1c27d. An average trader: 12,480 on his chest before the crash, 0 after it, then a small number that climbs slowly.
cast.Timmy: green shirt #43b05c, blue trousers #3a4a6b, red hair #d6402f under a cap with a brim, skin #f6d0a8. 212 on his chest, with a small gold '#1' badge while he is number one in town.
cast.Mr Gold: the richest man in town: gold shirt #f2b632, dark trousers #1f2433, black hair #1b1b1b, black sunglasses, skin #e8b88a. 1,000,000 on his chest in part 1, one billion after Moon Noodle. He has a gold plane and a gold sports car.
cast.Maya: the narrator's neighbour, a trader like him: pink shirt #e0457b, purple trousers #3a2f55, long dark hair #2b1a10, skin #c98b5e.
cast.the old neighbour: teal shirt #4fb3c9, brown trousers #55452f, grey hair #c9c9c9, skin #f3cfa6.
cast.the market sheriff: navy shirt with a gold star badge, a wide brown hat, a calm face. First seen in part 7.
cast.the town: toy-block sky blue and grass green, a road with a yellow line, block houses and trees; chest labels white with bold black numbers; gold for the rich, red for crashes and for numbers below zero, a dark red sky at each cliffhanger.

parts.lesson: Everyone sees a loss, and an average trader with a plan does about as well as holding the index.
parts.story: In this town, your money is printed on your chest by your trades: it climbs when you win, and when you lose, everyone watches it drop. Timmy lost everything on one stock, so now he is broke and holds out his hands to strangers for money. Some made fortunes, so they buy sports cars and fly round the world. I'm just an average trader with 12,480 on my chest, no better than holding the S&P 500. So I practise on Meme Street, where news moves made-up companies: I do the lessons and take every trade with a plan.
parts.cliffhanger: Then this morning, every number in town crashed to zero. Every one except Timmy's, which said number one. And he was standing at my door, smiling, holding something I'd never...

parts.lesson: Never put all your money into one stock, and a plan only works if you keep it while everyone else is buying.
parts.story: In my town your money is printed on your chest, and this morning every number hit zero except Timmy's. He was at my door with a battered notebook. Last night the whole town put everything into one stock, Moon Noodle, because Mr Gold, the richest man in town, said it could only go up. I broke my own plan and bought it too. By morning it was worth nothing. Timmy never bought: he lost everything that way once, so now he practises on Meme Street and writes every trade down. His chest said 212, and that made him number one in town.
parts.cliffhanger: Then he turned to the last page: everyone who sold Moon Noodle last night, right before it crashed. There was only one name on it, and when I read it...

parts.lesson: A pump and dump: someone talks a stock up so that he can sell it to you. Before you buy, ask who is selling, and why.
parts.story: In my town your money is printed on your chest, and the one man who sold Moon Noodle before it crashed was Mr Gold. He told the whole town to buy while he sold us every share he had, and that trick is called a pump and dump. We ran to the airport, but his gold plane was a dot in the sky, and his chest said one billion. Timmy said anger would not refill my chest, but a plan would. His first rule: before you buy, ask who is selling it to you, and why. We practised it on Meme Street, where news moves the prices, not one man shouting.
parts.cliffhanger: Three weeks later a shadow crossed the town. The gold plane was back, Mr Gold had a brand new stock, and the whole town lined up to buy it. And first in line was Timmy...

parts.lesson: A price that flies with no news behind it is hype. Check the reason before you buy, and never chase what has already gone up.
parts.story: In my town your money is printed on your chest, and the man who emptied every chest was back, selling a new stock called Turbo Hamster. Timmy was first in line, but not to buy. He asked one question, loud: if it is going to the moon, why are you selling it? Then he held up the chart. Turbo Hamster was already up nine hundred percent in a week, with no news at all. On Meme Street news moves prices, so I knew a price that flies on nothing is only hype. Half the line walked away. The other half borrowed money to buy more.
parts.cliffhanger: Then Mr Gold whispered in Timmy's ear, and Timmy's chest jumped from 212 to one million. He looked at me, said nothing, and walked onto the gold plane. And the door...

parts.lesson: Position size: never risk more than a small slice of your money on one trade, so one bad trade cannot take you out. Missing a gamble is not a loss.
parts.story: In my town your money is printed on your chest, and my only friend had just taken one million from Mr Gold and flown away. Turbo Hamster kept climbing. My neighbours' numbers doubled every day, and they laughed at the 95 on my chest. Every night I wanted to throw it all in. Instead I opened the notebook Timmy left on my doorstep. Rule two: never risk more than a small slice on one trade, so one bad trade cannot take you out. I practised it on Meme Street's Daily Chart until it was boring, and boring was the point.
parts.cliffhanger: Then an old photo fell out of the last page. Two young men in gold shirts, shaking hands in front of a gold plane. One was Mr Gold. And the other one was...

parts.lesson: A stop-loss: decide where you get out before you get in. And borrowed money can lose you more than you have.
parts.story: In my town your money is printed on your chest, and I had just found an old photo of Timmy shaking hands with Mr Gold. They were partners once, and the stock Timmy lost everything on was Mr Gold's first trick, played on him. Then Turbo Hamster began to wobble. Rule three in the notebook: decide where you get out before you get in. That is a stop-loss, and I had set a hundred of them on Meme Street. I showed my neighbour Maya, and she set one. That night Turbo Hamster crashed. Maya's stop sold early and kept most of her money, but the neighbours who had borrowed fell below zero, in red.
parts.cliffhanger: Then the gold plane landed in the middle of our street. The door opened and Timmy walked out, alone. His chest did not say one million any more. It said...

parts.lesson: Write every trade down: the record shows what really happened. And tricking people into buying so that you can sell to them is against the rules of a market.
parts.story: In my town your money is printed on your chest, and Timmy had just stepped off Mr Gold's plane with zero on his. He never kept the million. He took it to get on board, because Mr Gold keeps a notebook too: every pump, every dump, and every name he sold to. Timmy carried it straight to the market sheriff, because tricking people into buying so you can sell to them is against the rules. The sheriff locked Mr Gold's billion with a padlock, and the town cheered. It is why Timmy made me write down every trade on Meme Street: the record tells the truth.
parts.cliffhanger: Then Mr Gold laughed and pointed at Timmy. 'Ask your hero whose idea the very first pump was,' he said. The whole town turned, and Timmy looked at the ground and said...

parts.lesson: You do not need to be number one: spread your money, keep each trade small, know your exit and ask who is selling.
parts.story: In my town your money is printed on your chest, and Mr Gold had just told everyone that the first pump was Timmy's idea. Timmy said it was true. Years ago he thought of it, Mr Gold used it on him, and it cost him everything. Every coin he collected in the street since then went back to someone that trick had hurt. The sheriff shared out Mr Gold's billion, and every chest in town climbed back. Mine said 12,480 again: still average. But now I spread my money, keep each trade small, know my exit and ask who is selling, and I still practise on Meme Street every day.
parts.cliffhanger: Because average and still standing beats number one for a morning. And Timmy? He is still number one in this town, just not on his chest.
